spans.s:
khaṭvāṅga
(‘leg of a cot’)
------------------------------------------
Though the word literally means one of the four legs of a cot, it is used in a technical sense in the iconographical works, as a special kind of weapon held in the hand of शिव.
It is a magic wand made of the bone of the human arm surmounted by a skull. It is supposed to have invincible powers.
Persons who had committed grave sins were expected to go about naked and begging (for twelve years), holding this खट्वाङ्ग in hand and eating from the human skull-cup.
Terrible forms of शिव like the Kaṅkālamūrti are shown with the खट्वाङ्ग in one of their hands.
